title: Routing fanout annotator for region/tier fallback debugging
creator: Miguel Rivera
description:
Problem: When a request fans out across multiple routing options (region selection, tier routing, fallback model variants) engineers need an easy way to reconstruct why a particular path was chosen and how downstream fallbacks were invoked. Existing decision logs are sparse and either omit intermediate hop annotations or produce large unstructured blobs that are hard to query.

Goal: Implement a lightweight "fanout annotator" that annotates each routing hop with a small, structured decision event. Events will be persisted to the decision-events pipeline and surfaced in the Console trace view and per-route SLO dashboards. The annotator must be PII-safe, high-throughput (<2KB per event target), and support deterministic sampling for replay/forensics.

Scope:
- Instrument region selection, tier routing, and fallback model variant decisions made by the router.
- Produce per-hop annotations containing a stable decision key, hop index, selected option, rationale tags, cost estimate, local latency, and pointers to config snapshot and policy version.
- Add a thin enrichment service that attaches minimal model metadata and a diff-ish config id (no full policy dumps).
- Wire events into existing decision-events Kafka topic with topic schema versioning and an adaptive sampling header.
- Surface a condensed timeline in Console for sampled requests and enable download of full sampled decision stream for support/forensics.

Non-goals: full policy replication, permanent storage of full request payloads, or logging of user-provided prompt text beyond allowed redaction rules.
acceptance_criteria: Per-hop decision event emitted for >95% of sampled fanout requests
Sampling control supports deterministic sticky sampling for request families and probabilistic sampling adjustable from Console
Events contain config_snapshot_id and policy_version references without embedding full policy text
Events are PII-redaction compliant (no raw prompt text, no unredacted customer identifiers), verified by security review
Console shows a condensed fanout timeline for sampled requests and links to the raw event blob in S3 for authorized users
rollout_plan: Canary: enable for 0.5% of traffic in region-us-east-1 for 24h (monitor event volume and CPU)
Increase to 5% over 48h if metrics ok, then 25% for a week, then 100% rollout to hosted API; Dedicated customers opt-in by default disabled
Kill-switch: disable feature flag and retract in 5m via ops playbook
Post-rollout: run 7-day retention verification and a 30-day storage pruning job for full blobs
sample_payload_schema: Fields (flat): request_id, trace_id, span_id, hop_index, decision_key, selected_region, selected_tier, selected_model_variant, rationale_tags (comma-separated), cost_estimate_micros, latency_ms, config_snapshot_id, policy_version, sample_bucket, dt_iso. PII redaction: prompt_hash only; no raw prompt text. All fields are strings except numeric fields encoded as strings for transport. Events are compacted with snappy when persisted.
performance_constraints: End-to-end CPU overhead on router <5% at p99. Additional network egress for events <1% of request payload volume on average. Event serializer must avoid allocations in hot path (use object pool).
privacy_controls: Respect customer privacy flags: if customer.redaction_level == high then events use 'redacted' placeholders for model_variant and rationale_tags. Integrate with KMS policy to not include any unencrypted identifiers in long-term storage.
qa_steps: Unit tests for serializer and sampling logic
Integration test: spin up local Kafka+Enrichment service and verify event schema compliance
E2E test with synthetic fanout scenarios: region failover, tier preemption, model fallback (quantized variant) and assert timeline reconstruction matches expected hops
Security review: run static analysis and manual review of all emitted fields
Load test at 5x expected traffic with fanout_annotator enabled for 5% of traffic
comments: 2025-02-12 Miguel Rivera: Created ticket after oncall incident where a region fallback loop was hard to debug. Initial proposal drafted in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RIN/Fanout+Annotator

2025-02-18 Asha Patel: Design review with router and console teams. Agreed to keep per-event payloads compact and use a reference-based config_snapshot_id. Action: design enrichment service proto and topic schema.
2025-02-21 Danica Cho: Security reviewed initial field list; asked to remove unredacted customer_email and to include prompt_hash instead. Marked security_review_required=true.

2025-02-25 Asha Patel: Implemented serializer prototype. Benchmarks: median serialized size 740 bytes; 99th percentile 1.8KB. CPU overhead on router measured at ~2.7% at 1x QPS. Pushed branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/732

2025-03-01 QA: Integration test uncovered rare duplicate decision_key when router retries create new spans. Mitigation: include monotonic hop_index + request_family_id in decision_key. Added unit test coverage.

2025-03-04 Miguel Rivera: Ready to canary 0.5% in us-east-1 pending infra approval for topic partitioning (ENG-50217). Ops runbook drafted and uploaded: https://drive.redwood.ai/ops/fanout-annotator-runbook.md
next_steps: Merge serializer PR, deploy enrichment service behind flag, configure kafka topic partitions and retention, run canary in us-east-1, monitor event emit rate and storage cost. Follow-up ticket to add Console drill-down UI and RBAC for raw blob access.
